"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:

"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held. Don't look away from this."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you believe in."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."

"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I don't actually want to survive, whatever it takes. I want to belong somewhere. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else. Happy now?"

"Right. Go on, then."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."

"We lost Serwaa, Nadia, Onni, Sari, Jesmin and Fatima. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."

lastSay: d102: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. David Kim is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.

d102: 🕯️ David Kim is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d102: What David kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d102: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
